analysis.title: Brazil Energy: Government extends subsidies for diesel for one month
key_insights: Brazil's federal government extended for another 30 days the diesel subsidy for importers and producers. The BRL 2.12/liter incentive for both locally produced and imported diesel is unchanged.
Diesel imports remain eligible for an additional BRL 1.40/liter subsidy valid until November 6th. Total importer incentives are BRL 3.52/liter versus BRL 2.12/liter for local diesel.

GS estimates Petrobras' realized diesel price at BRL 5.43/liter (BRL 3.31/liter charged to distributors plus BRL 2.12/liter subsidy), about 25% below the international benchmark of roughly BRL 7.3/liter after yesterday's FX correction.

Because imported diesel is subsidized more heavily, distributors can buy imports at prices close to Petrobras' (about BRL 3.3/liter). GS says this asymmetry could reduce, but not eliminate, the scope for a Petrobras price hike.

GS assumes Petrobras keeps diesel prices unchanged through year-end, since it has limited visibility on whether the additional import incentive will expire or be renewed. A price hike would bring upside risk to GS's 4Q refining margin estimates.

For fuel distributors, the asymmetry reduces the competitive advantage of the largest players, which had been buying cheaper diesel from Petrobras in recent months. Petrobras prices are now similar to the import alternative.
GS remains Buy on Petrobras (PBR) for a roughly 20% dividend yield in 2027 at USD 75/bbl, assuming an extraordinary dividend next year.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays Buy on Petrobras for a roughly 20% dividend yield in 2027 at USD 75/bbl, assuming an extraordinary dividend next year. The diesel subsidy asymmetry limits scope for a price hike.

sector_views.rationale: The higher subsidy on imported diesel narrows the cost advantage large distributors had from buying Petrobras diesel, since local and import prices are now similar.

earnings_insights: GS assumes Petrobras holds diesel prices flat through year-end. A price hike would be an upside risk to GS's 4Q refining margin estimates (no figures given).
GS Buy rating on PBR rests on a roughly 20% dividend yield in 2027 at USD 75/bbl, assuming an extraordinary dividend next year (GS estimate).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Government incentive renewed unchanged for 30 days, supporting Petrobras' realized diesel price.
Together with the base incentive, importers receive up to BRL 3.52/liter. GS is unsure whether it will be renewed.
GS estimate: BRL 3.31/liter charged to distributors plus BRL 2.12/liter subsidy. About 25% below import parity.
GS estimate, already reflecting yesterday's FX correction. Import parity sits well above Petrobras' price.

risk_factors: The additional BRL 1.40/liter import subsidy may expire after November 6th or be renewed, and GS has limited visibility on which.
A Petrobras diesel price hike would raise refining margins above GS's 4Q estimates.
The subsidy asymmetry favoring imports may erode the competitive advantage of the largest fuel distributors.
